---
title: "Beans PCA: a recipe with no model"
bread-crumbs: false
---

The recipe is the product: extraction estimated on training data, judged on the validation set. No estimator anywhere. Ported from [Tidy Modeling with R, ch. 16](https://www.tmwr.org/dimensionality).

**Compare with R:** [side-by-side R ↔ Python](sbs/tmwr16-r-vs-py.html){target="_blank"} · R original: PC1–PC4 variance 59.4 / 24.4 / … (with orderNorm).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Port notes: gaps and parity vs the R original"}
```
The recipe IS the product: preprocessing estimated on training data, judged
visually on the validation set. No estimator anywhere.

PARITY NOTES:
 - step_orderNorm -> StepOrderNorm, step_pca -> StepPca(num_comp=4). Both are
   steps of the recipe, so the fitted recipe produces the PC scores itself.
   PC1-4 variance explained comes out as 59.44 / 24.42 / 6.95 / 5.44%, which
   matches R's 59.4 / 24.4 for the first two components.
 - R composes by piping MORE steps onto an already-prep()ed recipe and
   re-prepping; mlfeatures has no incremental fit. pca_rec is bean_rec plus
   StepPca, and is fit from the training data.
 - mlfeatures has no public accessor for a fitted step's loadings (R's
   tidy(id = "pca")), so the top-loadings table is not reproduced; variance
   explained is computed from the scores instead.
```
*Docs version loads the dataset from `mlfeatures.data`; the research originals
export these datasets from R's modeldata at first run.*
:::

## Specify

::: {#711b1e25 .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import polars as pl
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

from mlfeatures import (Recipe, StepDropZeroVariance, StepNormalize, StepOrderNorm,
                        StepPca)
from mlfeatures import Selectors as s

# ── Data

from mlfeatures.data import beans  # 13,611 x 17

# ── 3-way split (75 / 12.5 / 12.5, stratified by class)

bean_train, rest = train_test_split(
    beans, train_size=0.75, stratify=beans["class"],
    random_state=1601
)
bean_validation, bean_test = train_test_split(
    rest, train_size=0.50, stratify=rest["class"],
    random_state=1601
)

# ── Base recipe: zv -> orderNorm -> normalize

bean_rec = (
    Recipe(data=bean_train, target="class")
    .add(StepDropZeroVariance(s.numeric_features()))
    .add(StepOrderNorm(s.numeric_features()))
    .add(StepNormalize(s.numeric_features()))
)

# ── PCA recipe: the base recipe plus the extraction step

pca_rec = bean_rec.add(StepPca(s.numeric_features(), num_comp=4))
```
:::


## Fit

::: {#259c2b59 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
# fit() ~ prep(); transform() ~ bake(): the chapter doubles as the book's
# prep/bake tutorial, and this file doubles as mlfeatures's fit/transform one.
fitted = bean_rec.fit(bean_train)
bean_val_processed = fitted.transform(bean_validation)

pca_fitted = pca_rec.fit(bean_train)
```
:::


## Report

::: {#2887f5a0 .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
print("--- transformed validation head (zv -> orderNorm -> normalize) ---")
print(bean_val_processed.head())

scores = pca_fitted.transform(bean_validation)
print("\n--- validation-set PC scores (plot-ready) ---")
print(scores.head())

# ── Percent variance explained (R: tidy(id = "pca", type = "variance"))
# Each PC's variance on the training scores, over the total variance of the
# preprocessed training features.

total_var = (fitted.transform(bean_train).drop("class")
             .select(pl.sum_horizontal(pl.all().var())).item())
pct = (pca_fitted.transform(bean_train)
       .select((pl.col("^PC[0-9]+$").var() / total_var * 100).round(2)))
print("\n--- percent variance explained, PC1-PC4 ---")
print(pct)
```
